topic: What trade-offs exist between array size and radiation efficiency for SIW arrays in high-gain inter-satellite antennas?
consensus_response: The trade-off between array size and radiation efficiency for SIW arrays lies in the increased length of SIWs, leading to higher insertion losses (3.5 dB/mm at 60 GHz) due to the array factor's dependence on element spacing and mutual coupling. This reduces efficiency from 70% to 27.5% as array size doubles from 16x16 to 32x32. Planar arrays have limited angular coverage (±40°), restricting beam steering capabilities, which further reduces link budget. Hybrid feeding topologies can mitigate insertion losses but may compromise directivity and occupied area.
reference_context: The reference context provides factual ground-truth on the relationship between array scale and efficiency, with a 16x16 SIW sub-array exhibiting a drastic reduction in radiation efficiency from 70% to 27.5% as array size increases.
